name: conversus
description: Run competitive multi-agent deliberations — structured adversarial reviews, red-team proposals, and consensus building with game theory modes
long_description:
**Make better decisions by pitting AI agents against each other in structured debate.**

Instead of one LLM giving you a confident but unchallenged answer, conversus runs multiple agents with different perspectives through a structured adversarial pipeline. Weak arguments get exposed, disagreements get surfaced explicitly, and the final verdict is grounded in the full adversarial record.

## How it works

Every deliberation runs a **5-phase pipeline**:

1. **Review** — Each agent independently analyzes your question or document. No agent sees another’s work, forcing genuinely independent perspectives.
2. **Cross-Review** — Every agent reads every other agent’s review and identifies contradictions, tensions, and agreements. This is the adversarial core.
3. **Revision** — Each agent revises their position after reading the cross-reviews. They must explicitly withdraw, modify, or defend every recommendation — no dodging.
4. **Disputes** — Unresolved disagreements are extracted and structured: what the dispute is, who disagrees, and what evidence would settle it.
5. **Synthesis** — A neutral synthesizer reads the entire record and produces a final verdict that honors convergence, resolves disputes, and cites every claim back to the pipeline.

The result: a decision grounded in adversarial testing, not a single model’s confidence.

## Setup — your first deliberation in 30 seconds

No API keys needed to try it. The built-in **mock provider** runs a complete deliberation with synthetic responses so you can see the full pipeline shape before spending credits.

1. Open a new Claude Desktop chat
2. Paste: *"Help me decide whether to lease or buy a car. Use provider mock."*
3. Claude calls the tool, runs all 5 phases in milliseconds, and shows you the structured result

Once you’ve seen the pipeline shape, you’re ready for real deliberations.

**To use a real LLM provider**, go to the extension settings (Claude Desktop → Settings → Extensions → Conversus) and set your **Default Provider** to `anthropic` and add your **Anthropic API Key**. API keys are stored securely in your system keychain. Then just ask:

- *"Help me decide whether I should build a timber framed home or a conventionally framed home."*

No need to say "use provider anthropic" — the extension reads your configured default automatically.

## Try these prompts

- *"Help me decide whether I should build a timber framed home or a conventionally framed home."*
- *"I’m choosing between starting an LLC or an S-Corp for my freelance business. Run a conversus deliberation in red-blue mode."*
- *"Should I lease or buy my next car if I drive 15,000 miles a year and plan to keep it for 5 years?"*

No configuration needed — `conversus_decide` uses built-in pragmatist + devil’s advocate agents automatically. Just describe your decision and Claude picks the right tool.

## What’s included

**8 game theory modes:**

- **Cooperative** — agents seek convergence, surface integration issues
- **Winner-take-all** — each agent defends a position, synthesis picks one winner
- **Prisoner’s dilemma** — agents choose cooperate/defect, tests whether trust holds
- **Red-blue** — one team attacks, one defends (asymmetric adversarial review)
- **Negotiation** — agents negotiate terms with explicit offers and counteroffers
- **Resource-allocation** — agents compete for a fixed budget of attention/priority
- **Fair-division** — agents divide responsibilities or scope using fairness criteria
- **Mechanism-design** — agents propose and evaluate incentive structures

**3 tools:**

- `conversus_decide` — quick ad-hoc deliberation, no config file
- `conversus_run` — full deliberation from a YAML config with custom agents
- `conversus_validate` — check your config and see the cost before committing

**Also:**

- **10+ LLM providers** — Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, Gemini, Claude Code, and more
- **Self-contained** — no separate Python or pip install required. Claude Desktop’s bundled runtime handles everything.

## New to conversus?

See the [5-minute walkthrough](https://github.com/Build-Fractal/conversus-oss/blob/main/docs/user-guide/first-deliberation.md) — it runs a real deliberation and explains what you just saw.

Full documentation: [Desktop Extension guide](https://github.com/Build-Fractal/conversus-oss/blob/main/docs/user-guide/desktop-extension.md)

CONVERSUS_DEFAULT_PROVIDER.title: Default Provider
CONVERSUS_DEFAULT_PROVIDER.description: claude-desktop (uses your Claude session, no API key) | anthropic (direct API, needs key) | openai (GPT, needs key) | demo (free test mode)

CONVERSUS_DEFAULT_MODE.title: Default Mode
CONVERSUS_DEFAULT_MODE.description: cooperative (balanced) | winner-take-all (pick one) | red-blue (attack/defend) | prisoners-dilemma (test trust)

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.title: Anthropic API Key
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.description: Required when Default Provider is 'anthropic'. Get one at console.anthropic.com.

OPENAI_API_KEY.title: OpenAI API Key
OPENAI_API_KEY.description: Required when Default Provider is 'openai'. Get one at platform.openai.com.

GOOGLE_API_KEY.title: Google AI API Key
GOOGLE_API_KEY.description: Required when Default Provider is 'gemini'. Get one at ai.google.dev.

OLLAMA_BASE_URL.title: Ollama Server URL
OLLAMA_BASE_URL.description: URL for your local Ollama server (default: http://localhost:11434). Only needed if Ollama runs on a non-default port.

CONVERSUS_DISABLED_TOOLS.title: Disabled Tools
CONVERSUS_DISABLED_TOOLS.description: Comma-separated list of tool names to hide from this MCP server (e.g. 'conversus_login,conversus_run'). Disabled tools are not registered and don't appear in the tool list. Leave blank to expose all tools.

tools.name: conversus_decide
tools.description: Run an ad-hoc deliberation on a natural-language question using the built-in pragmatist + devil's advocate agents. Best for quick decisions — no config file needed. Accepts a mode parameter (cooperative, red-blue, winner-take-all, prisoners-dilemma).

tools.name: conversus_run
tools.description: Run or parse a full multi-agent deliberation from a YAML config file. Supports all 8 game theory modes, custom agents, target documents, and optional arbiters. Use this when you want reproducible deliberations with your own stakeholder personas.

tools.name: conversus_validate
tools.description: Validate a conversus YAML config and estimate the total LLM launch count BEFORE running. Catches schema errors, missing target files, and invalid mode names. Always run this before a real deliberation to know the cost.

tools.name: conversus_login
tools.description: Opens a browser for OAuth authentication with the specified provider. Stores the token locally so future deliberations use it automatically. Desktop Extension users: just say 'log in to anthropic' and the browser opens for authentication — no CLI needed.

tools.name: conversus_list_deliberations
tools.description: List past deliberations stored in the project's .conversus/deliberations/ directory. Returns deliberation names, timestamps, and summary metadata. Use this to browse deliberation history before reading individual files.

tools.name: conversus_show_deliberation
tools.description: Read a specific file from a past deliberation's output directory. Use after list-deliberations to inspect summaries, individual agent reviews, synthesis documents, or any other artifact produced during a deliberation.
